title: Voyager site adapter: folders
description: Where the `folders` primitive finds the site's sidebar, its conversation rows and the place its folder section goes. Page facts only: storage keys, buckets, account rules and Drive files stay in Voyager's per-site folder policy, so this section can never redirect folder data. A section that fails validation is dropped (the folders become unavailable) and `catalog:build` refuses to publish it.

format.description: Data format version; an unknown format drops the section.

sidebar.description: CSS selector of the site's sidebar root, searched in the document and observed for rows. Match nothing while the site lists no conversations: the folders then fall back to a floating panel.

transientSidebar.description: CSS selector matching an ancestor of the folder section while the sidebar shows only for a moment, such as a hover peek. The one-time folder guide waits until it no longer matches. Without it, the guide treats every shown sidebar as docked.

row.description: CSS selector of one conversation row.

link.description: CSS selector of the row's conversation link inside the row; the row itself when omitted.

title.description: CSS selectors inside the row tried in order for its title; the link's text when none has text.

pattern.description: Safe regex over the attribute value with exactly one capturing group, the id.

descendants.description: Read the attribute from the row's descendants too.

idSources.description: Where a row names its conversation before its link's route does.

observe.description: Attributes whose changes start a new pass over the rows.

portaled.description: CSS selector of rows the site renders outside `sidebar`, searched in the document.

drag.description: How a row is dragged onto a folder.

mount.description: Where the folder section is inserted.

id.description: The anchor's id, as the anchor preference stores it.

closest.description: Lifts the found element to its closest ancestor matching this selector, inside `sidebar`.

steps.description: Tried in order; the first that finds an element is where the section goes, just before it.

anchors.description: The anchors the section may sit before; ids are unique.

default.description: The anchor used unless the user chose another; must name one of `anchors[].id` (checked by the runtime reader, since standard JSON Schema cannot compare these values). The first anchor is used when omitted.

open.description: CSS selector present in the document while the sidebar is shown.

hideFiled.description: The rows hiding filed chats may hide. Without it, every `rows.row` may be hidden.

rows.description: CSS selector of the rows that may be hidden.

keepShown.description: CSS selectors of rows never hidden.

rowMenu.description: The row's own menu, which gains a Move to folder entry.

trigger.description: CSS selector of the row's menu button.

menu.description: CSS selector of the open menu.

item.description: CSS selector of one menu item.

open.description: How the menu is seen to open: `aria-expanded` on the trigger flips, or a press starts a short look.

template.description: CSS selector of the item cloned for the entry.

strip.description: Attributes removed from the cloned item.

iconHolder.description: CSS selector of the element whose glyph becomes the folder icon.

plainItem.description: Index of the rename item among the menu's plain items.

page.description: Title rules for the open conversation. Required by the shared folder section on catalog sites; Voyager's own sites (AI Studio) title prompts from their own pages.

placeholderTitles.description: Titles the site shows before a chat is named; never stored as a title.

byLanguage.description: Placeholders by UI language, such as `zh-CN`.

fallbackLanguage.description: The `byLanguage` entry used for an unlisted UI language.

titleSuffix.description: Safe regex removed from `document.title` to leave the conversation's title. A tab title it does not match is the site's own page, never a conversation's title.

newChat.description: CSS selector of the site's own new-chat link.
